rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 4 (kp 2.6, base_speed 1.2, kd 0.8) scored 679.86, just below iteration 3 (683.18). The oval stayed 20/20 (mean 1.83 s) and the s-bend fell to 19/20 (one off-track, mean 2.13 s). The slalom is still 0/20, but its max_error dropped from 0.0646 to 0.0618 and its line_loss_events held at 1.0, down from 1.45. So lowering corner gain and speed helped the slalom without breaking the other tracks. The slalom is still 0.0018 m above the 0.06 m limit, and every slalom failure is still an off-track end. Geometry has not changed since iteration 2, and the Evaluator asked to keep it fixed until the controller question is settled.

Change. kd 0.8 to 0.9, with kp 2.6, base_speed 1.2, ki 0.05, sensor_weights, line_loss and all geometry unchanged. The slalom alternates left and right, so extra derivative damping should cut overshoot between bends and pull max_error below 0.06. This is the next lever named in iteration 4's Evaluator feedback. Oval steering_oscillation was 0.14 at kd 0.8, so the jitter cost of higher kd should be small.

Expected result. Slalom max_error between 0.055 and 0.06, some slalom finishes, slalom line_loss_events at or below 1.0, oval still 20/20 with completion_time under 2.0 s, and s-bend finish rate at or above 0.95.

Decision rule for the next iteration. If the slalom max_error falls below 0.06 with any slalom finishes, hold these values and test a small ki change (0.05 to 0.1) only if line losses stay high. If the slalom still ends off track with max_error at or above 0.06 and kd 0.9 does not reduce it, return kd to 0.8 and test kp 2.4 at base_speed 1.2. If the s-bend or oval finish rate drops below 0.95, return kd to 0.8.

Hypotheses to test. (a) Higher kd reduces slalom overshoot enough to bring max_error under 0.06. (b) Slalom failures come from overshoot on alternating bends, not from speed alone. Measurements requested: full set, read per track, especially slalom max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation.
